request: why can a magnifying glass burn paper in sunlight?

beats.intent: Parallel sunbeams falling on a lens held above a sheet of paper
beats.narration: Sunlight falls on a magnifying glass held above a sheet of paper.
beats.code:
stage.title("Focusing sunlight")
lens = Ellipse(width=5.0, height=0.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3).move_to([0, 1.0, 0])
paper = Rectangle(width=6, height=0.15, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to([0, -2.5, 0])
beams = VGroup(*[Arrow([x, 2.8, 0], [x, 1.25, 0], buff=0, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=3) for x in np.linspace(-2.2, 2.2, 6)])
stage.play(FadeIn(lens), FadeIn(paper), LaggedStart(*[GrowArrow(b) for b in beams], lag_ratio=0.1))
stage.add(lens, paper, beams)

beats.intent: The beams bending through the lens and meeting at a small bright spot on the paper
beats.narration: The lens bends every beam towards one small spot on the paper.
beats.code:
spot = np.array([0, -2.4, 0])
rays = VGroup(*[Line([x, 0.9, 0], spot, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=3) for x in np.linspace(-2.2, 2.2, 6)])
stage.play(Create(rays))
dot = Dot(spot, color=WHITE, radius=0.1)
stage.play(GrowFromCenter(dot))
stage.add(rays, dot)

beats.intent: Two squares compared: the 5 cm wide patch of light caught by the lens and the 0.5 cm spot it lands on
beats.narration: Light collected over a lens five centimetres wide lands on a spot half a centimetre wide.
beats.code:
big = Square(2.5, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.15).move_to([4.5, 1.2, 0])
small = Square(0.25, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to([4.5, -1.6, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(big), FadeIn(small))
stage.add(big, small)
stage.label(big, "5 cm", direction=UP, color=YELLOW)
stage.label(small, "0.5 cm", direction=DOWN, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The squares beside (5 / 0.5)² = 100 times as much light per square centimetre
beats.narration: The width shrinks ten times, so the area shrinks a hundred times: a hundred times the sunlight on each bit of paper, enough to scorch it.

request: which is better value: 500 g for £2.00 or 750 g for £2.70?

beats.intent: Two packs drawn as boxes: 500 g at £2.00 and 750 g at £2.70
beats.narration: One pack is five hundred grams for two pounds. The bigger one is seven fifty for two seventy.
beats.code:
stage.title("Better value?")
small = Rectangle(width=1.6, height=2.0, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.4).move_to([-3, -0.3, 0])
big = Rectangle(width=2.2, height=2.6, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.4).move_to([0.5, 0, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(small), FadeIn(big))
stage.add(small, big)
stage.label(small, "500 g, £2.00", direction=DOWN, color=BLUE)
stage.label(big, "750 g, £2.70", direction=DOWN, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: Each pack split into 100 g pieces: 5 pieces and 7.5 pieces
beats.narration: Compare the price of the same amount: a hundred grams. The small pack has five of those, the big one seven and a half.

beats.intent: Bars of price per 100 g: 40p and 36p
beats.narration: Two pounds over five is forty pence per hundred grams; two seventy over seven and a half is thirty six.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
b = draw_bars(stage, [40, 36], labels=["small", "big"], color=ORANGE)
stage.caption("pence per 100 g")

beats.narration: The big pack is better value, by four pence every hundred grams.

request: why is the angle in a semicircle always 90 degrees?

beats.intent: A semicircle on a diameter AB with a point C on the arc and the triangle ABC
beats.narration: Draw a semicircle on a diameter A B, and pick any point C on the curve.
beats.code:
stage.title("The angle in a semicircle")
O = np.array([0, -1.5, 0])
R = 3.0
arc = Arc(radius=R, start_angle=0, angle=PI, color=GREY_B).move_arc_center_to(O)
A, B = O + R * LEFT, O + R * RIGHT
t = ValueTracker(2.0)
C = lambda: O + R * np.array([np.cos(t.get_value()), np.sin(t.get_value()), 0])
tri = always_redraw(lambda: Polygon(A, B, C(), color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.2))
dotC = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(C(), color=YELLOW))
stage.play(Create(arc))
stage.add(tri, dotC)
stage.play(FadeIn(Dot(A)), FadeIn(Dot(B)))
stage.label(A, "A", direction=LEFT)
stage.label(B, "B", direction=RIGHT)

beats.narration: The angle at C is always a right angle.
beats.code:
mark = always_redraw(lambda: RightAngle(Line(C(), A), Line(C(), B), length=0.3, color=YELLOW, quadrant=(1, 1)))
stage.add(mark)
stage.play(Create(mark))

beats.intent: C sliding along the arc, the right-angle mark staying
beats.narration: Slide C anywhere along the curve, and it stays ninety degrees.
beats.code:
stage.play(t.animate.set_value(0.6), run_time=2)
stage.play(t.animate.set_value(2.6), run_time=2)
stage.caption("C moves; the angle stays 90°")

beats.intent: The centre O joined to C, splitting the triangle into two isosceles triangles
beats.narration: Why: join the centre to C. O A, O B and O C are all radii, so both small triangles are isosceles. Their angles add to make the angle at C exactly half of a hundred and eighty.
beats.code:
oc = always_redraw(lambda: Line(O, C(), color=GREEN))
stage.add(oc)
stage.play(Create(oc))
stage.equation(r"2a + 2b = 180^\circ", r"\Rightarrow a + b = 90^\circ")

request: how do batteries add up in a torch?

beats.intent: One 1.5 V battery drawn as a cell
beats.narration: One battery gives one and a half volts.
beats.code:
stage.title("Batteries in series")
cell = lambda: VGroup(Rectangle(width=1.6, height=0.7, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5), Rectangle(width=0.15, height=0.3, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.9).shift(0.875 * RIGHT))
one = cell().move_to([-4, 1.2, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(one))
stage.add(one)
stage.label(one, "1.5 V", direction=UP, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: Four batteries end to end, plus to minus
beats.narration: Put four end to end, the plus of each touching the minus of the next.
beats.code:
four = VGroup(*[cell() for _ in range(4)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.05).move_to([0, -0.6, 0])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(c) for c in four], lag_ratio=0.2))
stage.add(four)

beats.intent: A brace over the row labelled 6 V
beats.narration: Their pushes add up: four times one and a half is six volts.
beats.code:
br = Brace(four, UP, color=GREEN)
stage.play(GrowFromCenter(br))
stage.add(br)
stage.label(br, "6 V", direction=UP, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: The row beside 4 × 1.5 V = 6 V, and a bulb glowing brighter
beats.narration: Twice the voltage of three cells, so a bulb made for six volts glows properly.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"4 \times 1.5 = 6\ \text{V}")
bulb = Circle(radius=0.4, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.9).next_to(four, DOWN, buff=0.5)
stage.play(FadeIn(bulb))
stage.add(bulb)
